subject: 2021 Preliminary Election and Early Voting Schedule
overview: The Council approved the official order and polling locations for the 2021 preliminary and municipal elections, alongside a designated schedule for in-person early voting. The body also voted to expand the Zoning Board of Appeals and addressed infrastructure petitions including a debated ADA ramp for Citizens Bank.

items.title: MIT 25th Anniversary Recognition
items.summary: The Council commended the Medford Invitational Tournament and its Challenger Baseball program for 25 years of service to children with mental and physical challenges.

items.title: Eagle Scout Commendation: Desmond Lambert
items.summary: Desmond Lambert was recognized for attaining the rank of Eagle Scout and completing a service project at the Medford dog park.

items.title: 2021 Preliminary Municipal Election Order
items.summary: Approved the official call and designated polling places for the preliminary election on September 14 and the municipal election on November 2.

items.title: In-Person Early Voting Schedule
items.summary: Approved four days of in-person early voting for the preliminary election and five days for the municipal election. A motion to reduce the preliminary early voting window to two days failed after the Council debated administrative costs versus voter access.

items.title: Zoning Board of Appeals Expansion
items.summary: Approved an ordinance amendment expanding the board from three members to five and adding two associate members with staggered terms.

items.title: Laundromat License: 281 Boston Avenue
items.summary: Approved a cleaning and dyeing license for GNC LLC doing business as a laundromat.

items.title: Grant of Location: Citizens Bank ADA Upgrades
items.summary: Tabled a petition for a sidewalk ramp at 257 Spring Street because the Council required guidance from the city engineer and assessor on whether to charge a licensing fee for the use of public land.

items.title: Utility Grants of Location
items.summary: Approved two conduit installations for National Grid on Boston Avenue and Magoon Avenue, and one for Verizon on Boston Avenue to service the Green Line Extension station.

items.title: Labor Peace Agreements for Cannabis Dispensaries
items.summary: Referred a resolution seeking labor peace agreement language in cannabis host community agreements to the City Solicitor for a legal opinion on council authority.

items.title: Abutter Notification for Tree Removals
items.summary: Referred to the Committee of the Whole a proposal to require 14-day advance notice to abutters before the removal of city-owned trees.

items.title: Personnel: Retirement and Condolences
items.summary: Recognized the retirement of Deputy Fire Chief Fran Fusco after 34 years and offered condolences to the families of former Treasurer Mary D. DeFranzo Coletta and employee Frances Gianetti.

items.title: Infrastructure and Maintenance Updates
items.summary: Requested administrative updates on the bicycle infrastructure master plan, ride-share (TNC) fee allocations, and the status of an ongoing private investigation into allegations by the former CFO.

items.title: DCR Maintenance and Utility Safety
items.summary: Approved requests for DCR to create guardrail openings at Duggar Park and perform weed cutting on Route 16, and requested the relocation of a utility pole obstructing a sidewalk on Boston Avenue.

items.title: Personnel Ordinance Third Reading
items.summary: Passed to take its third and final reading a series of personnel ordinance amendments.
